fmt <- function(x, d = 0) if (!length(x) || all(is.na(x))) "[pending]" else formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
num <- function(x, f = "%.3f") if (!length(x) || all(is.na(x))) "[pending]" else sprintf(f, x)
pv <- function(x, f = "%.0f") if (is.null(x) || !length(x) || all(is.na(x))) "[pending]" else sprintf(f, x)
pthr <- function(p) if (!length(p) || is.na(p[1])) "[pending]" else if (p[1] < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", p[1])
stars <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p <= 1e-4, "****", ifelse(p <= 0.001, "***", ifelse(p <= 0.01, "**", ifelse(p <= 0.05, "*", "")))))
acv <- function(term, model = "M3", dep = FALSE, col = "estimate") ACOEF[[col]][ACOEF$model == model & ACOEF$dependence == dep & ACOEF$sample == (if (dep) "with previous year" else "all years") & ACOEF$term == term]
ac  <- function(term, model = "M3", dep = FALSE, col = "estimate") { x <- acv(term, model, dep, col); if (col == "p") pthr(x) else num(x, "%+.3f") }
aft <- function(model, dep = FALSE, col = "aic", sample = if (dep) "with previous year" else "all years") AFIT[[col]][AFIT$model == model & AFIT$dependence == dep & AFIT$sample == sample]
wc  <- function(model, term, col = "estimate") { x <- W16[[col]][W16$model == model & W16$term == term]; if (col == "p") pthr(x) else num(x, "%+.3f") }
xws <- function(col, fun = mean, f = "%.1f") if (is.null(XWSUM)) "[pending]" else pv(fun(XWSUM[[col]]), f)
uwt <- function(weight, ring, col, f = "%+.3f") { x <- if (is.null(UWTEST)) NULL else UWTEST[[col]][UWTEST$weight == weight & UWTEST$ring == ring]; if (col == "p") pthr(x) else pv(x, f) }

# Methods S1

The wind component of the MicroMet model of @liston2006 is seven equations, implemented directly from the source paper with its equation numbers given below.

Terrain slope $\beta$ and slope azimuth $\xi$ came from the elevation model, equations 12 and 13 of @liston2006. Curvature $\Omega_c$ is a cell's elevation minus the mean of the two opposite cells one curvature length scale away, taken on four direction lines and averaged, their equation 14, and the length scale was estimated as the first lag at which elevation autocorrelation fell below 0.5, which was `r V$eta` here. Assigning $\theta$ to wind bearing, slope in the wind direction was computed as follows

$$\Omega_s = \beta \cos(\theta - \xi)$$ {#eq-slope}

with $\Omega_s$ and $\Omega_c$ each scaled to $[-0.5,\,0.5]$. The terrain weighting factor applied to the observed speed $W$ was derived using

$$W_w = 1 + \gamma_s \Omega_s + \gamma_c \Omega_c, \qquad \gamma_s = \gamma_c = 0.5$$ {#eq-weight}

This provided the basis for calculation of the terrain-modified speed using

$$W_t = W_w W$$ {#eq-speed}

and a diversion of wind direction computed as

$$\theta_d = -\tfrac{1}{2}\, \Omega_s \sin\!\left[2(\xi - \theta)\right].$$ {#eq-divert}

By @eq-weight, $W_w$ depends on direction and not on speed, so it was computed once for each of 16 wind direction sectors of 22.5 degrees, the sixteen points of the compass, and each hourly observation was multiplied by the surface for its own sector, so that nothing was averaged before the terrain acted on it, and over all sectors $W_w$ ran from `r sprintf("%.2f", V$mm_ww[1])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", V$mm_ww[2])`.

# Methods S2

The wind and heat terms of section 2.3 of the main text rested on these sources. Convective lift was the velocity scale of @deardorff1970 from the ERA5-Land sensible heat flux [@munozsabater2021] and the ERA5 boundary layer height [@hersbach2020]. Back-trajectories were computed with HYSPLIT [@stein2015] on the North American Regional Reanalysis [@mesinger2006]. Sun on each slope under each hour's cloud came from r.sun in GRASS GIS [@suri2004], and afternoon air temperature from microclima [@maclean2019microclima].

Three groups of terms that the earlier models lacked were added beside M3 and E2. Valley bottoms and ridge tops were measured by the multiresolution indices of valley bottom and ridge top flatness [@gallant2003], computed in SAGA GIS on the 30 m elevation model. Canopy height was the 2017 lidar surface model less its bare-earth model at 1 m, summarised to each 30 m cell as its mean, its standard deviation and the share of the cell above 5 m, and because the lidar was flown after the outbreak it measured the canopy that remained. Winter cold was the lowest daily minimum temperature and the number of days at or below -30 °C in the winter, October to April, that ended before the flight behind each map, from the ERA5-Land daily minimum [@munozsabater2021] moved to each cell's elevation at the lapse rate the reanalysis cells gave on that day, with the cooling that cold air draining into the cell would add, from the basins, flow accumulation and drainage model of microclima [@maclean2019microclima], on every day whose night met that package's conditions for cold-air drainage at the site. Over the ten winters the temperature rose with elevation, an inversion, on `r xws("inversion_share", f = "%.2f")` of days, the conditions for drainage held on `r xws("cad_share", f = "%.2f")` of nights, drainage cooled the coldest cells by up to `r xws("coldpool_min", fun = function(x) abs(mean(x)))` °C, and the lowest winter minimum across the study area averaged `r xws("tmin_mean")` °C and fell no lower than `r xws("tmin_low", fun = min)` °C, so that the days at or below -30 °C, `r xws("cold_days_mean", fun = max)` on average in the coldest winter, did not enter the models. The sixteen-day model was also refitted with the terms of the annual model it lacked, northness, sky view, the wind shelter index, convergence and stand age, and with the station pressure of each period, the flight-hour departure from each station's May to September mean and its three-hour change, for the period and for the same period one year earlier.

The source of each year's attack was the red crowns of the year before, whose brood had come through the winter in those trees. Winter survival was computed for every 30 m cell with the cold tolerance model of @regniere2007cold, in the R code of @goodsman2024code, from ERA5-Land daily temperature [@munozsabater2021] moved to each cell's elevation and converted to phloem temperature [@bolstad1997modelling]. Around each cell the share of cells attacked the previous year, weighted by survival, was computed within 150 m and from 150 to 1,050 m in eight compass sectors. Each sector was weighted by the share of flight hours the wind blew from it at the Akokli Creek station, and the upwind and downwind shares were compared by a Wald test of the difference between their coefficients.

# Results S1

With the previous year's attack and the dependence terms in the annual model, valley bottom flatness entered at `r ac("mrvbf", "M3 valley and ridge flats", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("mrvbf", "M3 valley and ridge flats", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`) and ridge top flatness at `r ac("mrrtf", "M3 valley and ridge flats", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("mrrtf", "M3 valley and ridge flats", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), cold-air pooling at `r ac("coldpool", "M3 cold-air pooling", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("coldpool", "M3 cold-air pooling", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), mean canopy height at `r ac("chm_mean", "M3 canopy height", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("chm_mean", "M3 canopy height", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), its variation at `r ac("chm_sd", "M3 canopy height", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("chm_sd", "M3 canopy height", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`) and the share above 5 m at `r ac("chm_cover", "M3 canopy height", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("chm_cover", "M3 canopy height", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`). The lowest minimum of the winter before the flight entered at `r ac("wlag_tmin", "M3 winter cold", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("wlag_tmin", "M3 winter cold", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), and with the summer held at `r ac("wlag_tmin", "M3 winter cold with year", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("wlag_tmin", "M3 winter cold with year", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`). In the sixteen-day models with the previous period's attack, valley bottom flatness entered at `r wc("E2 valley and ridge flats", "mrvbf")` (`r wc("E2 valley and ridge flats", "mrvbf", "p")`), ridge top flatness at `r wc("E2 valley and ridge flats", "mrrtf")` (`r wc("E2 valley and ridge flats", "mrrtf", "p")`), cold-air pooling at `r wc("E2 cold-air pooling", "coldpool")` (`r wc("E2 cold-air pooling", "coldpool", "p")`), mean canopy height at `r wc("E2 canopy height", "chm_mean")` (`r wc("E2 canopy height", "chm_mean", "p")`) and the winter minimum at `r wc("E2 winter cold", "wlag_tmin")` (`r wc("E2 winter cold", "wlag_tmin", "p")`). With the terms of the annual model added to the sixteen-day model, northness entered at `r wc("E2 annual terms", "northness")` (`r wc("E2 annual terms", "northness", "p")`), sky view at `r wc("E2 annual terms", "sky_view")` (`r wc("E2 annual terms", "sky_view", "p")`), the wind shelter index at `r wc("E2 annual terms", "wind_shelter")` (`r wc("E2 annual terms", "wind_shelter", "p")`), convergence at `r wc("E2 annual terms", "convergence")` (`r wc("E2 annual terms", "convergence", "p")`) and stand age at `r wc("E2 annual terms", "PROJ_AGE_1")` (`r wc("E2 annual terms", "PROJ_AGE_1", "p")`). The pressure departure of the previous summer's period entered the lagged model with dependence terms at `r wc("E2 lagged with pressure", "preslag_anom_flight")` (`r wc("E2 lagged with pressure", "preslag_anom_flight", "p")`) and its three-hour change at `r wc("E2 lagged with pressure", "preslag_tend_flight")` (`r wc("E2 lagged with pressure", "preslag_tend_flight", "p")`).

In the flight window the late-morning surface temperature of north-facing ground was `r num(STSM$st_north_mean, "%.1f")` °C against `r num(STSM$st_south_mean, "%.1f")` °C on south-facing ground, averaged over the ten summers and `r fmt(STSM$scenes)` scenes, and it correlated `r num(STSM$r_northness_mean, "%.2f")` with northness and `r num(STSM$r_radiation_mean, "%.2f")` with modelled flight-window radiation (Figure S14). With the measured temperature of the previous summer in place of modelled radiation, northness entered at `r ac("northness", "M3 measured heat")` (`r ac("northness", "M3 measured heat", col = "p")`) against `r ac("northness", "M3 lagged wind")` (`r ac("northness", "M3 lagged wind", col = "p")`) beside radiation, and temperature itself at `r ac("st_flight_lag", "M3 measured heat")` (`r ac("st_flight_lag", "M3 measured heat", col = "p")`). With the three terms from the 1 m terrain added to the lagged model, ground roughness within the cell entered at `r ac("lid_rough_1m", "M3 lidar")` (`r ac("lid_rough_1m", "M3 lidar", col = "p")`), the share of the cell facing north at `r ac("lid_north_share", "M3 lidar")` (`r ac("lid_north_share", "M3 lidar", col = "p")`) and the spread of crown-scale position at `r ac("lid_tpi_55m_sd", "M3 lidar")` (`r ac("lid_tpi_55m_sd", "M3 lidar", col = "p")`), and the AIC moved from `r num(aft("M3 lagged wind"), "%.0f")` to `r num(aft("M3 lidar"), "%.0f")`.

Attack upwind of a cell did not raise its attack more than attack downwind. In the survival-weighted model the two shares within 150 m did not differ (`r uwt("survival", "near", "p")`), from 150 to 1,050 m the upwind share entered at `r ac("srv_up_far", "M3 upwind and downwind sources")` against `r ac("srv_down_far", "M3 upwind and downwind sources")` downwind, a difference of `r uwt("survival", "far", "difference")` \[Wald z = `r uwt("survival", "far", "z", "%.2f")`, `r uwt("survival", "far", "p")`\], and splitting the shares by wind direction raised the AIC from `r uwa("survival", "aic_undirected")` to `r uwa("survival", "aic_directional")`. Every specification is listed with its estimates in Tables S11 and S12.
